title: The closed–open coefficient embedding is monic
statement: Let $T,Z$ be schemes and $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $V\subset T$ be open with inclusion $j$, and let $i:Z\to T$ be a closed immersion whose image is $T\setminus V$. Put $J=\operatorname{Injective.under}(j^*F)$ and let $a:j^*F\hookrightarrow J$ be its chosen injective embedding. Then the pair of the adjoint transpose $\eta_j\circ j_*a:F\to j_*J$ and the unit $\eta_i:F\to i_*i^*F$ is a monomorphism $F\to j_*J\oplus i_*i^*F$. Here $j^*,i^*$ are inverse images, $j_*,i_*$ direct images, and $\eta$ denotes the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction unit.

source.place: Tag 0F07, proof of condition (3): The closed–open coefficient embedding is monic

proof.text: A morphism into F killed by the pair is killed by each component. Under adjunction, its open restriction followed by the chosen injective embedding is zero, so its open restriction is zero by cancellation of the monomorphism. The closed component similarly kills the closed restriction.

The algebraic-closure residue-field points of V and Z, composed with the two inclusions, cover T. Pullback-stalk comparison makes the morphism zero on each such point. The conservative family of geometric stalks therefore makes the morphism zero. The cancellation-of-zero criterion proves that the pair is monic. This argument is fully realized by the Lean proof.
